slides.title: Follow the ownership boundary
slides.takeaway: Library: Windowed rows, grouping, search UI and per-row interaction.
slides.notes: The library owns Windowed rows, grouping, search UI and per-row interaction. The host owns Ordered data, active route, storage changes and action implementations.  The arrows show data/callback direction, not an implicit network request. The documented isolation rules and known implementation deviations are listed in qa-report.md.

cards.title: Transfer surfaces
cards.body: Transfer queues and rename dialogs are separate public components.

slides.notes: Customization comes from the current exports and prop declarations. Stable row data: Items carry title, source, pinned state and optional unread/task badges. Action extension: getActions and onActionMenuOpen inject row actions. Transfer surfaces: ImportExportQueue and RenameConversationPopup are separate exports. For UI, import the package stylesheet and use documented props or stable public classes. A component-level color override and inherited theme tokens are different levels of control. Locale strings and direction should be supplied by the host; do not introduce app i18n into a reusable library.

slides.title: Constraints that affect integration

cards.title: Preserve ordering
cards.body: The host supplies an already-ordered flat list.

cards.title: Selection is not routing
cards.body: onSelectConversation returns an id for the host to interpret.

cards.title: Virtualized content
cards.body: Only a subset of rows exists in the DOM at a time.

slides.notes: Review these constraints before choosing the library. Preserve ordering: The host supplies an already-ordered flat list. Selection is not routing: onSelectConversation returns an id for the host to interpret. Virtualized content: Only a subset of rows exists in the DOM at a time.
